Muro is the factory: muro/, prompts/ and muro_build.py. It holds no package-specific knowledge.

requirements.text: Muro is a standard-library-only Python 3.10+ factory separate from the packages it builds (such as examples/marionette/), emitting standalone multi-host coordinators across Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode and Hermes with no package-specific rules leaked into muro/ or prompts/.

requirements.text: sources.json defines the package identity (slug, name, command, version, optional description, install_policy, language, and stack rules), parameterizing dist/<slug>/, /<command>, NOTICE.md, GUIDE.html, and .<slug>/map.md while rejecting hardcoded .muro/ paths when slug != 'muro'.

evidence.excerpt: muro_build.py fails closed if plugin.slug or plugin.command is empty, non-kebab-case, or matches a reserved host command.

requirements.text: muro_build.py prevents naming collisions across three levels: stripping upstream public commands, enforcing unique capability IDs and per-source script namespaces (scripts/<source-id>/), and rejecting reserved native host commands or colliding installed plugins.

evidence.excerpt: The gate must keep failing closed on any change to the license terms.
A source may declare license_path, a plain repository-relative file path.
Every source declares pin, one of: release, head, static.

requirements.text: muro_build.py --check-sources verifies every source's 40-character commit SHA, declared pin mode (release tag, upstream head, or static commit), MIT or Apache-2.0 license (root or scoped license_path with nested-license checks), and UTF-8 non-binary selected_paths; --offline-pins validates manifest pins and local repositories while explicitly disclosing skipped remote fetches.

evidence.excerpt: The current schema has ten mandatory frontmatter fields; the router remains six columns.

requirements.text: Capabilities carry 10 mandatory frontmatter fields (id, role, when, after, outputs, checks, intents, tools, hooks, conflicts), optional reads, needs and output_types fields, and a mandatory ## Sources section, mirrored in a 6-column ROUTER.md (id | role | when | after | outputs | intents) and strictly validated with unknown frontmatter keys rejected.

evidence.excerpt: Harmonizer AI synthesizes knowledge and chooses coherent responsibilities, merges, alternatives, real prerequisites and conflict resolutions.

requirements.text: Intake, harmonization and runtime task classification are performed semantically by the host LLM from source and catalog meaning; manifest order, matching labels, regex and keyword lists never decide merges, precedence or runtime routing.

evidence.excerpt: every output key has exactly one producer in a resolved plan.
Repeated capabilities in one plan use explicit step_id: <cap>#<n> with namespaced output keys.

requirements.text: Python validates the host AI's explicit selections against task, stack constraints, catalog digest, conditional needs judgments, role variants, declared conflicts and single-owner outputs (supporting explicit step_id instances with namespaced outputs), failing closed without automatic substitution.

evidence.excerpt: Every successful build generates GUIDE.html for that release, at the package root and in each of the five independently installable host skill directories.

requirements.text: Every release generates an offline, self-contained GUIDE.html (defaulting to English, or Italian via plugin.language) embedding the verified Cytoscape.js bundle, declared after/needs/reads relationships and validated guide-examples.json scenarios without browser-side task classification.

evidence.excerpt: Maps track map_status (active or completed)... step validates outputs and batched checks in memory before publishing a single atomic state snapshot.

requirements.text: One-step tasks execute in direct mode whenever no active map exists, while multi-step maps support inline/stdin JSON, atomic step batches (outputs + checks), selective upstream preservation (--preserve-completed), token-bound lock recovery (unlock --token), and map completion (complete) restoring direct mode.
